🙏 A Prayer of Encouragement for Secretary Vince Dizon 🙏

*thank you for sharing*

Heavenly Father,

We bring before You Secretary Vince Dizon, a man called to lead our nation’s roads, bridges, and flood-control works with purpose. At this moment when the DPWH is facing the weight of scrutiny over numerous flood-control projects involving ghost works, substandard materials, and misused funds, yet flooding still worsens, grant him wisdom beyond his years.

Lord, give him courage to root out entrenched wrongs, clarity to identify where system flaws enabled ghost or incomplete flood structures, and integrity to stand firm even when the winds of criticism blow.

We pray also for peace in his heart. Despite the pressure of leading reform in the face of unfair practices, may he always know that the people support his role and trust in his vision for a clean and effective DPWH. May each project he advances reflect genuine service to every Filipino, especially those who live in flood-prone communities.

Finally, Lord, protect him from weariness and disillusionment. Surround him with a team that shares his upright mission. May his leadership be a beacon of the new, transparent, and accountable Philippines we believe in… guided by our love for country and anchored in the vision of President @bongbongmarcos for a #BagongPilipinas.

In Your name we pray.

Amen. 🙏🇵🇭

📸 CTTO

TRAFFIC ADVISORY 

24 OCTOBER 2025

ROADS AFFECTED BY THE CAF CHAMPIONS LEAGUE MATCH BETWEEN ORLANDO PIRATES FC AND SAINT-ELOI LUPOPO IN ORLANDO, SOWETO

Motorists are advised to be aware of traffic disruptions around Orlando Stadium for the CAF Champions League match between Orlando Pirates FC and Saint-Eloi Lupopo in Orlando, Soweto, Saturday, 25 October 2025.

Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD) officers will be deployed to ensure the free flow of traffic around Orlando Stadium and to ensure the safety of all road users. 

The following routes will be affected:

N17, Soweto Highway, Klipspruit Valley Road, Martha Louw Street and Mooki Street.

Road closures will be implemented at 11h00.

Road closures will be implemented on: 

Mooki Street between Nkom Ya Hlaba and Masopha Streets. Also, expect closures on Martha Louw Street between Klipspruit Valley Road and Mooki Street, and at Adams and Rathebe Streets next to the YMCA and Adams and Nzama Streets

The following alternative routes can be used in the affected areas: 

From Mooki Street, motorists can use Ballenden and Masopha Street. Motorists can also use the Soweto Highway and Klipspruit Valley Road.

Parking for spectators will be at an open space by the corner of Martha Louw Street and Klipspruit Valley Road, Shomane High School, AB Quma Primary School (Scott Street), Lofentse Girls High School (Mooki Street), Zithathele Primary School (Mooki Street), Leratong Primary School, Orlando High School, Selelekela High School (Mooki Street), Lereche Primary School Adams Street), Orlando Rugby Field (Adams Street), and Orlando Court (Mooki Street). VIP’s, Media, and VOC members' parking will be inside Orlando Stadium.

Residents and members of the public are urged to exercise patience for the duration of the match as we are expecting traffic disruptions in the area.

Gates will open at 12h00, and the kick-off will be at 15h00, so it is appealing for spectators to arrive early to avoid congestion before the match.

We are further appealing to road users to acquaint themselves with the traffic management for the day so they can plan their routes accordingly.

Ends.

Issued by the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department's Communications Unit. #JoburgRoadSafety #JHBTraffic #SaferJoburg #NomakanjaniManjeNamhlanje

TRAFFIC ADVISORY
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 

24 OCTOBER 2025

CAF CONFEDERATION CUP MATCH - KAIZER CHIEFS FC vs AS SIMBA FC 

The Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD) urges residents and commuters to be aware of significant traffic disruptions in Dobsonville, Soweto due to the CAF Confederation Cup soccer match between Kaizer Chiefs FC and AS Simba FC at Dobsonville Stadium on Sunday, 26 October 2025

We urge all attendees and the surrounding community to take note of the planned traffic management operations, road closures, and parking arrangements. Heavy traffic volume is anticipated in the vicinity of the stadium.

The match is expected to start at 15:00 and the gates will be opened at 12:00.

JMPD will deploy officers from 11:00 to ensure the safe, free, and fast flow of traffic around Dobsonville Stadium. Motorists should anticipate and plan for road closures and regulated traffic at the following key intersections:

Road Closures will be implemented at 11:00:

 * Marambu Street & Mondi Street
 * Marambu Street & Mngadi/Tati Street
 * Marambu Street & Sifuba Street

Traffic will be actively controlled at intersections including, but not limited to:

 * Main Street & Marambu Street
 * Main Street & Luthuli Street
 * Main Street & Ellias Motsoaledi Street
 * Luthuli Street intersections (Dzana, Msikana, Gwele, Majova Streets)

Spectators are strictly prohibited from parking on the pavement, the shoulder of the roadway, or on the street. All vehicles that contravene the Road Traffic Management Act will be impounded.

Designated spectator parking areas are:

 * Dobsonville Rugby Field (Access via Main and Luthuli Street, Majova Street, and Sifuba Street)

 * Dobsonville Swimming Pool (Access via Marambu/Mondi Street and Main Street)

 * Kopanong Community Hall (Also for ticket sales, if not sold out)

Important Access Information:

 * Emergency vehicles, team buses, and staff vehicles will use Marambu/Mondi Street.

 * VIPs, Media, and VOC members will access parking at the main gate of the stadium.

 * Dobsonville residents opposite the stadium must display valid access cards with their house number and name clearly visible.

The JMPD, alongside SAPS and other stakeholders, will be highly visible to maintain law and order.

We appeal to all motorists to exercise patience, follow the instructions of all deployed law enforcement and traffic officials, and adhere to the designated parking and traffic plans.

-ENDS-
#SaferJoburg #JoburgRoadSafety #JHBTraffic #NomakanjaniManjeNamhlanje

$GRAB & Why Telecom is going to WIN🔥🔥🔥

Grab Holdings Limited , Southeast Asia's leading AI SuperApp, launched "Partner Apps" on October 21, 2025, a feature that integrates third-party services directly into the Grab app for seamless booking and payment without leaving the platform. Among the initial five partners is Firsty, a global telecommunications provider specializing in eSIMs (embedded SIMs). This allows Grab users to instantly purchase and activate mobile data plans for over 180 countries, including key Southeast Asian markets, bypassing traditional SIM swaps, local carrier hassles, or expensive roaming fees.

The Offer: Users access Firsty's eSIMs via a dedicated "Partners" tab in the Grab app. Plans activate immediately upon purchase, with data coverage tailored for travel ( 1GB/day for short trips). New users get 100% cashback on their first eSIM purchase through Grab until the end of 2025, redeemable via GrabRewards (soon rebranding to GrabCoins).

Pricing and Integration: Costs match Firsty's direct rates (starting ~$5–$10 for basic plans), paid via GrabPay (with credit/debit and PayLater options rolling out soon). Users earn GrabRewards points on every transaction, redeemable across Grab's ecosystem (rides, food...).

Availability: Live now in Singapore and Malaysia, expanding to Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, and beyond in the coming months. It's positioned as a "travel essential" for Grab's 46 million monthly transacting users.

This isn't Grab building its own telecom infrastructure (like a full MVNO); it's a low-friction partnership leveraging Grab's distribution to embed telecom as a value-add service. Similar to past integrations (Globe prepaid WiFi in the Philippines in 2021), it capitalizes on Grab's 200M+ app downloads and high tourism traffic.

Why Grab is going to win with this intergration!

1. Low-Friction for massive user growth

~Affordable Telecom Plans:Firsty's eSIM plans start at low prices (~$5–$10 for basic plans), making them an accessible entry point for users, especially tourists and first-time Grab app users. The 100% cashback offer (via GrabRewards, soon GrabCoins) until the end of 2025 further lowers the barrier, incentivizing users to try GrabPay for these transactions.

~Seamless Payment Integration: Users must pay for eSIMs via GrabPay (credit/debit or PayLater options), directly exposing them to Grab's fintech infrastructure. This is particularly effective for the 90%+ of Southeast Asia's 700M population who are underbanked and may not regularly use digital payments, where telecom demand is a necessity. 

2. Targeting High-Intent Users:

~Tourist Segment: Tourists, who make up 20–25% of Grab’s mobility volume, are a prime target. They’re more likely to need instant connectivity (eSIMs) and are less price-sensitive, spending 70% more on premium services. By requiring GrabPay for eSIM purchases, Grab captures these high-intent users, many of whom may not have used GrabPay before.

~Cross-Selling Opportunity: Once users link a card or try PayLater for telecom, they’re more likely to use GrabPay for other services (rides, food, delivery), as it’s already set up. Data from Grab’s pilots shows multi-service users spend 4–5x more, with fintech adoption boosting retention by 2x.

3. Ecosystem lock-in:

~Low-cost telecom hints users to think more affordable services to be available on the same SuperApp will lead to more services' purchases. This mirrors strategies like WeChat’s, where small transactions ( red packets) drove payment adoption. Grab’s AI-driven personalization pushes relevant prompts ( PayLater for eSIMs), increasing conversion.

~Network Effects: More GrabPay users strengthen the ecosystem, attracting more partners (like Firsty or redBus) and merchants, which in turn drives further GrabPay usage. This flywheel could help GrabPay capture a larger share of Southeast Asia’s $180B digital payments market (growing 15% YoY).

4. Growth is what @AnthonyPY_Tan wants!

~Grab should have a much higher Transacting Users growth in the coming months/quarters. This telecom strategy can accelerate transacting user to x3 x4, much higher than Dine-Out due to the nature of low-cost telecom. 

More Users=More cross-selling= Higher Rev Growth

~Fintech Growth: Grab’s fintech arm (GFin) grew loan disbursements 81% YoY in 2024. Low-cost telecom purchases via PayLater or GrabPay Wallet will accelerate this, with fintech potentially contributing 30–40% of Grab’s $3.37B revenue by 2026 (vs. 20% now). New GrabPay users will also see Buy Now Pay Later, small loan, GrabUnlimited and other offers that are too attractive to ignore.

~Profitability Boost: Fintech services have higher margins (60–80%) than mobility/delivery (20–30%). Scaling GrabPay usage through telecom could lift adjusted EBITDA margins much higher.

Conclusion: Offering low-cost telecom services is a deliberate strategy to onboard new GrabPay users, leveraging the high-frequency, high-intent tourist segment and underbanked locals. It’s a low-risk, high-reward move to grow GrabPay’s user base and transaction volume, reinforcing Grab’s fintech ambitions and ecosystem dominance. Expect 30–40% YoY growth in GrabPay adoption tied to such initiatives, compounding Grab’s 30%+ overall revenue growth in a $1T+ digital economy.

Anthony Tan wants GrabPay to be the main payment system in SEA, he is pushing the boundaries to give users the best discount/experience. This will also create more income opportunity for Merchants/Drivers partners, aligning with "Secret Sauce" and "Secret Weapon". The strategy that currently winning 75% market share and will soon to dominate 90-95% market share.  Grab near-term stock price action may be manipulated, but short sellers are afraid of solid fundamental, that is improving at a rapid pace. Executions in the last 3 months have been outstanding with mostly low-cost high reward Organic services. At the end of the day, it is a SuperApp where it is treating Users/Merchants/Drivers as customers, and it is very difficult to lose with this "Secret Sauce"

$GRAB Officially Launched Telecom & Car-rental🔥

I have been talking about Aggressive Tourism Expansion, and @AnthonyPY_Tan is going ALL IN! It is very clear that, $GRAB plans to take the whole tourism market(152m tourists). The level of execution in the last 60 days is incredible, too many partnerships to talk about. I had followers asked if Telecom was possible, now it is. These intergrated services will be expanded beyond Malaysia and Singapore in the coming months.  

Philipp Kandal, Chief Product Officer at Grab, said: “With Partner Apps available natively within Grab’s app, users will get more out of using Grab than ever. Partner App services complement our users’ lifestyles and needs beyond Grab’s on-demand offerings. Users can enjoy a seamless all-in-one-place app experience through their existing Grab accounts and payment preferences, without downloading any additional apps. At the same time, Partner App brands can leverage Grab’s app and platform to engage our 46 million users and boost their own reach across Southeast Asia. Users across our markets can look forward to seeing many more brands they know and love as Grab Partner Apps in the coming months.”

5 new services added onto Grab SuperApp, but I will talk about just 2 new services:

Firsty: A telecommunications provider that offers a global eSIM with instant data abroad. With Firsty’s eSIM, travelers can stay connected without changing SIM cards, switching to local plans, or data roaming. The eSIM can be purchased through Grab Partner Apps for use internationally in over 180 countries, including Grab markets across Southeast Asia. New Firsty users purchasing an eSIM through Grab will receive 100% cashback until year end.

DriveLah: A peer-to-peer car-sharing platform available in Singapore that lets users instantly book and unlock nearby cars using their phone. Every trip is fully insured and supported 24/7. Users will get 33% off (up to SGD $88) for their first DriveLah booking through Grab, as per terms and conditions, until year end.

Vince Vissers, Founder of Firsty, said: “We’re thrilled to partner with Grab to make staying connected effortless. Grab users can now always stay online with Firsty, no local SIMs, no roaming surprises, just internet connection that follows you everywhere.”

Dirk-Jan ter Horst, Co-founder of DriveLah, said: “Being available natively within the Grab app means millions of users can discover DriveLah without downloading another app or creating a new account. With keyless access and comprehensive insurance, renting a nearby car becomes as simple as ordering a ride. We’re proud that Grab has chosen DriveLah as a partner to bring car sharing to millions of users in Singapore.”

[Traffic Advisory] NOTICE OF ROUTINE MAINTENANCE ON M1 AND M2 MOTORWAYS

@MyJRA wishes to inform road users of the routine maintenance currently underway on the M1 (northbound and southbound) between Grayston Drive and Shakespeare Avenue Bridge, and on the M2 (eastbound and westbound) from Lower Germiston Road to Main Reef Road. Roadwork will be active until the 30th of October 2025.

Lane closures will be effected from 09h30 - 15:00 during weekdays and between 07h30 – 16h00 on weekends.

Traffic delays are expected along the M1 and M2 sections during the maintenance period, therefore motorists are advised to plan their journey in advance, exercise caution on the roads and reduce their travelling speed for the safety of our maintenance teams and other road users.  We thank all road users in advance for their patience and cooperation.
